sections.html:
SeaTac is a small, fast-growing city south of Seattle, built around the region's main airport. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 34,578 people, a 10.0 percent jump over the 2020 base. Older neighborhoods such as Angle Lake, Bow Lake, McMicken Heights and Riverton Heights predate the city's 1990 incorporation. Owners live in fewer than half of the homes, and typical values sit well below Seattle's.

Renters fill many SeaTac homes, which means plenty of sellers are landlords or heirs of a rental. If that fits you, the rental section below comes first.

Almost every parcel in SeaTac is touched by the airport, and buyers know it. Sea-Tac International sits on roughly three square miles inside city limits, owned and run by the Port of Seattle, and the city's boundaries wrap around it. Noise complaints in the 1960s and 1970s led the Port and King County to the Sea-Tac Communities Plan of 1976, the first program in the country where an airport operator bought homes and school buildings near the airport and soundproofed others. Around 420 acres of vacated land north of the field became North SeaTac Park, with fields, trails and a community center.

Buyers will bring up noise and flight paths, so decide ahead of time what you will say about both. The roof deserves a look as well. On the state disclosure form, one question covers any roof leak during the past five years, and an old leak should be repaired or reported before the house goes on the market.

Written records help here. If you ever received sound insulation or other work tied to the airport, or have receipts for new windows, keep copies in your sale folder. They show a buyer that the house has been looked after and may answer a noise question before it is asked.

sections.h2: Transit and schools buyers ask about
sections.html:
Commuters like the city's links. Link light rail stops at SeaTac/Airport station and Angle Lake station. King County Metro runs the RapidRide A Line on International Boulevard (State Route 99) and the RapidRide F Line on Southcenter Boulevard. State Route 518 and the Airport Expressway tie the city into the freeway system, and some Sound Transit Express buses end at the airport and nearby hubs.

Highline Public Schools covers most of the city. Most residents are zoned to Chinook Middle School and Tyee High School, some go to Sylvester Middle School and Highline High School in Burien, and residents north of the airport are generally zoned to Glacier Middle School and then Highline High School. Small parts of SeaTac are in the Kent School District and the Renton School District. If your house sits near a boundary, confirm the district before you give buyers an answer.

Light rail and RapidRide stops give some SeaTac streets a clear selling point. Name the nearest station or bus line in your listing, along with the commute of 25.4 minutes that the average resident faces, and let buyers do the math for their own workplace.

sections.h2: If your SeaTac house is a rental
sections.html:
A business license is required to run a rental unit in SeaTac, and the city points owners to the Washington Department of Revenue for the online application. Each tenant must also receive the city's Renting in SeaTac Guide, a handout on rights, evictions, deposits, repairs and notices.

Ending a tenancy so you can sell follows its own statute. For a single-family rental, RCW 59.18.650 calls for 90 days of written notice. After the tenant moves out, the owner has 30 days to start selling in earnest, typically by listing at a reasonable price or advertising on the multiple listing service. If the home goes back on the rental market or comes off the market inside 90 days, the law assumes there was never a plan to sell. Tenants removed in violation may recover whichever is greater, actual damages or three months of rent, plus fees and costs.

Also call the city of SeaTac before listing to find out whether any code complaint or unfinished permit sits on the address.

sections.h2: Closing costs for a SeaTac seller
sections.html:
Excise tax is the largest cost, and Washington puts it on sellers in the usual case. A buyer inherits the duty when the seller leaves it unpaid, and the balance may become a lien. The state tiers are 1.1 percent up to $525,000, 1.28 percent up to $1,525,000, then 2.75 percent and 3 percent. Starting with sales on January 1, 2027, the first break rises to $551,000. King County layers a local rate over the state's.

Money goes to the county treasurer at the time of sale, with the notarized deed date as the date the Department of Revenue uses. Interest builds on late payments. Call the King County treasurer to learn the SeaTac local rate and your property tax balance, and have escrow explain how the year's property tax is divided with the buyer.

A seller disclosure statement is part of every standard sale here. The buyer receives it within five business days of contract acceptance, then gets three business days to rescind. Look for questions on easements, shared driveways, sewer hookups, wood stoves, drainage, shorelines, wetlands, floodplains and critical areas.

Costs are easier to manage when you know them early, so ask escrow for a rough estimate of your net proceeds before you commit to a closing date.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale worth considering?
sections.html:
For some owners it is. Think about it if the house needs work, a tenant lives in it, or a title or tax issue would trip up a buyer relying on a loan. Measure each offer against what a listing would leave you after repairs, excise tax and months of carrying costs.

  • Get the closing date and the split of escrow and title charges in writing.
  • Round up permits and receipts for additions or major repairs.
  • Disclose tenants and the lease term before you sign anything.

The path is short. Once you accept, escrow opens and a title search runs. Proceeds pay off any loan, you sign the deed with a notary, and the county gets the affidavit and tax. Funds are released after recording. Nobody orders an appraisal or lender review, so your timetable is set by title work and your own plans.

Gather the deed, a loan payoff statement and your latest King County tax statement before the first conversation, so you can answer questions without delay.

faqs.q: How many people live in SeaTac, Washington?
faqs.a: About 34,578 as of July 1, 2025, compared with 31,454 in the 2020 census. Roughly 46.5 percent of homes are lived in by their owners.

faqs.q: Do I need a business license to rent out a house in SeaTac?
faqs.a: Yes. SeaTac requires one for any rental unit, and the application is online through the Washington Department of Revenue. Tenants must be given the city's Renting in SeaTac Guide.

faqs.q: Which school district is SeaTac in?
faqs.a: Highline Public Schools serves most of the city, mainly Chinook Middle School and Tyee High School. Small parts are in the Kent and Renton districts, so check your address.

faqs.q: How much notice must I give a tenant if I want to sell the house?
faqs.a: For a single-family home, RCW 59.18.650 requires 90 days of written notice. After the tenant leaves, list or advertise within 30 days at a reasonable price, or the law assumes you never meant to sell.

faqs.q: What is the state excise tax on a SeaTac sale?
faqs.a: Four state tiers apply: 1.1 percent to $525,000, 1.28 percent to $1,525,000, 2.75 percent to $3,025,000 and 3 percent beyond, plus a local rate. Break points shift for sales beginning January 1, 2027.
